metadata.title: AI stocks hold steadier after Nvidia says it still sees strong growth ahead

content.text:
NEW YORK (AP) — The sharp drops for Nvidia and other stocks tied to the artificial-intelligence industry appear to be easing on Wednesday, at least for now, which is helping to steady Wall Street following its four-day losing streak.
The S&P 500 rose 0.2%. The strength for tech stocks had the Nasdaq composite up 0.5% as of 9:35 a.m. Eastern time, but the rest of the market was not doing as well. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dipped 172 points, or 0.3%.
Nvidia once again was at the center of the market's moves. The chip company's stock rose 0.9% after it reported stronger profit and revenue for the latest quarter than analysts expected. Perhaps more importantly, it also gave a forecast for revenue in the current quarter that was better than expected.
The question is whether Nvidia's big growth can continue following the turmoil created by the sudden downfall of Jensen Huang, its former CEO and co-founder. He had an immense personality that drew attention and investment to AI, and he built Nvidia into a company so big that it helped to fund some of the industry's growth itself.
"Our momentum is real," Nvidia's interim CEO, Colette Kress, told investors and financial analysts after announcing the company's latest results. "Our demand is accelerating. Our supply is growing. Our customers and our partners are with us. And employees are committed. We've got this."
For now, at least, the encouraging numbers and words coming out of Nvidia helped to support several other stocks in the industry.
Broadcom, a rival chip company, added 1.2%. Advanced Micro Devices rose 1.2%.
But CoreWeave, which buys Nvidia chips and rents access to them out to customers over the cloud, dropped 4.3% after coming into the day with a loss of more than 30% for the year so far.
The entire industry has been swinging with waves of concerns recently. Besides criticism that AI stock prices simply shot too high in their frenzy, the industry is also facing worries that this month's sweeping victories for Democrats in the U.S. midterm elections could mean more regulation for it.
Elsewhere on Wall Street, stocks of big retailers were mixed following mostly strong profit reports.
TJX climbed 7.3% after the company behind the TJ Maxx and Marshalls stores reported slightly better earnings for the latest quarter than analysts expected. CEO Ernie Herrman said he expects momentum to accelerate through the holiday shopping season.
Target rallied 4.1% following a better-than-expected profit report, which included its strongest quarterly sales gain in roughly five years.
